messages.subject: multidimensional containers
parts:
Consider the vector container,

vector<matrix<Type> > V(a);

where each element is equal to, 

matrix<Type> m(i,j);

Is it possible to extend V into higher dimensions,
such that V could be indexed as,

V(a, b, c, ..., z)( , ), 
where V(a, b, c, ..., z) is of type matrix<Type> with i rows and j cols

Effectively what i'm asking is whether the "vector" container 
can be transformed into a "multidimensional array" container,
with the constraint that the objects in the container are either
matrix or vector types.


Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Chris

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: multidimensional containers
parts:
Starting from your vector of matrices

vector<matrix<Type> > V(a);

you can construct an array of matrices like this:

array<matrix<Type> > A(V, d);

Here, d is the dimension attribute, e.g.

vector<int> d(3);
d << 2,3,4;

There is no limitation on the array dimension, however the multi dimensional array access A(i,j,k,...) is only implemented up to dimension 7:

https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/structarray.html

One more question.

It all seems to work fine except when using the REPORT macro.

Is this a bug, or does the REPORT macro not yet support array containers such as those described previous?

Here is some example code that fails:
#include <TMB.hpp>
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() (){
  
PARAMETER(theta);

vector<int> d(3); d << 2,2,2;
int a = d(0)*d(1)*d(2);

matrix<Type> m(1,5); 
m << 1,2,3,4,5;

vector< matrix<Type> > V(a);
array< matrix<Type> > A(V,d);

for(int i=0; i<2; i++)
  for(int j=0; j<2; j++)
    for(int k=0; k<2; k++)
      A(i,j,k) = m*i*j*k;

REPORT(A);

return theta;
}

note, if you call REPORT on an element of A the example works.

Thanks again for all of your help,

Chris
